title: Leave a useful support trail
summary: Write records that help the next technician.

passages.heading: The core idea
passages.markdown: A support ticket is a working record of a problem, its impact, and the actions taken. Capture the affected user and device, the exact symptom, the start time, and the business effect. Severity describes impact rather than how strongly a user phrases the request. Use clear factual language and record observable results so another technician can continue without asking the user to repeat everything. Include only the information needed for the support task.

passages.heading: In the real world
passages.markdown: Progress notes should connect an action to its result: what was checked, what changed, and what was observed afterward. A resolution note should explain the fix and how functionality was verified. Asset records connect equipment identifiers to ownership, warranty, licensing, and life-cycle information. A knowledge-base article turns a repeatable resolution into reusable guidance with scope and prerequisites. Avoid placing passwords, recovery codes, or unnecessary personal data into tickets. Follow organizational handling rules and escalate with enough context for the receiving team to act safely.

passages.heading: Make it stick
passages.markdown: Put it into practice by explaining the decision in your own words. In a support scenario, identify the requirement first, connect it to the relevant technology, and check the result against that requirement. If the evidence changes, revisit your reasoning rather than repeating the same action. Document what you observed so the next person can understand your conclusion.
